answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because sparrow only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice glacier is enforced by the ledger itself: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any lotus approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
